primary_unique_answer_proof: A is uniquely impossible. Its base from (0,0) to (2,0) forces at least one contained square to have that entire horizontal side: squares contacting y=0 only at a vertex cannot cover an interval, while any horizontal square side of length 2 contained in x in [0,2] is the whole base. The roof apex (1,3) must belong to the second square. Both supporting roof rays have slopes +/-1, so a square fitting this right-angle apex has adjacent side endpoints x=1 +/- sqrt(2), outside [0,2]. B is the union of a side-2 axis square centered at (5,sqrt(2)) and a side-2 square rotated 45 degrees about the same center. C combines the side-2 diamond with bottom (10,0) with a side-2 upright square whose top is y=2+sqrt(2). D uses two upright side-2 squares shifted (1,1); E uses two side-2 squares shifted (1,0).
